cites.quote: At inference the weights are frozen, which is why one copy in GPU memory can serve many users at once
query = bank's row × W_Q, where W_Q is a learned matrix shared by every token
A weighted average mixes several vectors, each multiplied by its share
Each head gets its own softmax, so it can focus sharply on its own target.
the letters inside each piece are not part of the input
A 100-token answer means about 100 passes through the machine, one per new token.
What the model learns from “the river flooded” carries over to “the stream flooded”.
A gradient says, for each number, how much the error would change if that number moved a little.
Training the model later can't fix it, because the tokenizer is frozen first.
The same token always reads the same row; context is added later, by attention.
100,000 rows × 4,096 numbers ≈ 410 million learned numbers, just for this table.
IDs are labels, not quantities.
Weights are the learned numbers (the embedding table and everything else); they change only during training.
The matrices are weights (frozen in use); each query, key and value is an activation.
the model keeps a second learned table with one row per token
bank is used in both water and money sentences, so it ends up between the two clusters.
reordering the words hands attention the same vectors
The same cause breaks reversing words, rhyming, and arithmetic on long numbers.
Characters make sequences long, and attention cost grows with the square of length.
double the tokens, ×4 the scores
raise e to each score, then divide each by the total
multiplies two vectors position by position and adds the results into one number
raise e to each score, then divide each by the total
Every token scores itself and every earlier token
start from single bytes, then repeatedly merge the most frequent neighbouring pair into a new token
Shares must sum to 1 because the next step is an average.
Languages it saw less of get fewer merged pieces, so the same meaning takes more tokens, down to raw bytes in the worst case.
Whole words need millions of entries and fail on any unseen word.
Score = query · key, softmax, then blend the values.
Scores are divided by √(vector size) before softmax so they don't grow too large.
Separate learned matrices let each job be tuned on its own.
A self-join done as a nested loop: every row compared with itself and every earlier row.
A number multiplied by 0 has no influence, so it never moves.
a second table with one row per slot (a hard length limit)
n(n+1)/2 scores for n tokens, about n²/2
Heads split the width rather than adding to it: 32 heads × 128 numbers = 4,096.
More tokens means higher cost (billed per token), slower generation (one token per step), less room in the context window
push river and stream in the same directions, so their rows drift together over billions of examples

flags.note: 'e' (Euler's number) used as the base of the exponent with no explanation beyond the ≈2.718 in Go deeper; fine for engineers but unexplained why e.
'matrix' and 'W_Q × row' multiplication used without any step teaching matrix-vector multiplication; also 'residual connection' mentioned in passing.

Triangle grid axes labelled 'tokens it scores' / 'token doing the looking' with no per-cell label; the 'later token, not seen' grey is explained only in legend, and Q23-style self-attention (diagonal) is not marked distinctly.
'MLP', 'layer', 'scores' used in the diagram before any step teaches them; MLP deferred to Lesson 2.
